families.title: A multiplication fact
explanations: fact-slip (recall): A multiplication fact (12 × 12) is not yet reliable.
add-for-multiply (conceptual): 12 × 12 was added instead of multiplied.

teach.idea: a × b counts a groups of b: the same as b groups of a.
teach.method: Rebuild a fact from one you know: double, add or take away one group, or split a factor.

families.title: Area of a rectangle
explanations: perimeter-for-area (conceptual): The distance around (perimeter) was found instead of the space inside (area).
fact-slip (prerequisite): A multiplication fact (12 × 12) is not yet reliable.
add-sides (conceptual): The two sides were added; area multiplies them.

teach.idea: Area counts the unit squares that cover a shape.
teach.method: A rectangle has rows of equal squares: rows × squares in a row.

families.title: A missing part of an equivalent fraction
explanations: additive-scaling (conceptual): The same amount was added to the top as to the bottom; equal fractions multiply both by the same number.
scale-one-part (procedural): Only the bottom was changed; the top must be multiplied by the same number.
fact-slip (recall): A multiplication fact (9 × 10) is not yet reliable.

teach.idea: Equal fractions cover the same amount: cutting every piece into k smaller pieces multiplies top and bottom by k.
teach.method: Find what the bottom was multiplied by, and multiply the top by the same number.

families.title: Adding or subtracting like fractions
explanations: add-denominators (conceptual): The bottom numbers were added too; they name the size of the pieces, which does not change.
multiply-tops (procedural): The top numbers were multiplied; adding fractions adds the pieces.
subtract-reversed (procedural): The smaller top number was taken from the larger one the wrong way round.

teach.idea: Like fractions count the same size of piece: add or take away the pieces.
teach.method: Add or subtract the tops; the bottom (the size of the pieces) stays.

families.title: The definite integral of a constant
explanations: fencepost-width (procedural): The whole numbers from a to b were counted (one too many); the width is b − a.
add-width-height (conceptual): Width and height were added; the area multiplies them.
fact-slip (prerequisite): A multiplication fact (12 × 4) is not yet reliable.
forget-height (conceptual): Only the width was found; the area is width × height.
ignore-lower-limit (conceptual): The width was taken as the upper limit only; the width is upper minus lower.

teach.idea: The integral of a constant c from a to b is the area of a rectangle: width b − a, height c.
teach.method: Width (upper minus lower) times height.

families.title: A quadratic equation with whole-number roots
explanations: root-signs (procedural): The numbers in the brackets were taken as the solutions; (x − 2) = 0 gives x = 2, so the signs flip.

teach.idea: If a product is zero, one of its factors is zero.
teach.method: Factorise x² + px + q = (x − r)(x − s), then each bracket gives a solution.

families.title: A value on a straight line
explanations: concatenate (conceptual): 9x with x = 9 was read as the digits 99; 9x means 9 × x.
add-for-multiply (conceptual): 9x was worked out as 9 + x; it means 9 × x.

teach.idea: y = mx + c gives y for any x: m × x, then add c.
teach.method: Multiply m by the value of x first, then add (or subtract) c.

families.title: Where a line meets y = x², by trying whole numbers
explanations: square-as-double (conceptual): x × x was worked out as x + x (doubling); x × x is x squared.

teach.idea: Where two graphs meet, their y values are equal.
teach.method: Try each whole number and compare x × x with the line's value.

families.title: Which graph is higher at a point

teach.idea: A graph is higher at x when its y value there is larger.
teach.method: Work out both y values at that x and compare.

families.title: The area between a parabola and a line
explanations: line-only (conceptual): The area under the line was found; the region is between the line and the parabola.
wrong-order (procedural): The parabola was taken as the top curve; here the line is above, so the answer was negative.

teach.idea: The area between two curves is the integral of (top − bottom) between where they meet.
teach.method: Find where they meet, check which is on top, integrate the difference.

families.title: A power of a whole number
explanations: one-factor-short (procedural): One factor too few was multiplied: 12 must appear 4 times.
multiply-for-power (conceptual): A power was worked out as a multiplication (12⁴ as 12 × 4); a power multiplies 12 by itself 4 times.
add-for-power (conceptual): The two numbers were added; a power is repeated multiplication.

teach.idea: aⁿ multiplies a by itself n times.
teach.method: Multiply step by step: 3, 9, 27, 81 for 3⁴.

families.title: Expanding a(x + b)
explanations: first-term-only (procedural): Only the x was multiplied by 12; the number outside multiplies every term in the bracket.
add-for-multiply (conceptual): 12 and 12 were added; the bracket means 12 × 12.
fact-slip (prerequisite): A multiplication fact (12 × 12) is not yet reliable.

teach.idea: The number outside a bracket multiplies every term inside.
teach.method: Multiply along an arrow to each term.

families.title: Expanding (x + a)(x + b)
explanations: product-for-sum (conceptual): The two numbers were multiplied for the x term; 8 × 9 is the number at the end, and the x term collects 8x and 9x.
one-cross-term (procedural): Only one of the two middle products was kept; both x × b and a × x give an x term.
sign-slip (prerequisite): -1 + 9 was worked out without the signs; adding numbers with different signs is a difference.

teach.idea: (x + a)(x + b) has four products; two of them are x terms.
teach.method: The x coefficient is a + b and the constant is ab.

families.title: The derivative of k xⁿ at a point
explanations: power-not-multiplied (procedural): The power was lowered but not brought down as a factor: the derivative of xⁿ is n xⁿ⁻¹.
value-not-slope (conceptual): The function's value was found, not its rate of change (the derivative).
power-not-lowered (procedural): The power was not lowered: the derivative of xⁿ is n xⁿ⁻¹.
multiply-for-power (prerequisite): A power was worked out as a multiplication (3⁴ as 3 × 4); a power multiplies 3 by itself 4 times.

teach.idea: The derivative of k xⁿ is k n xⁿ⁻¹.
teach.method: Multiply by the power, lower it by one, then substitute.

families.title: The definite integral of k xⁿ
explanations: no-divide (procedural): The power was raised but not divided by: ∫ xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹ ⁄ (n + 1).
differentiated (conceptual): The function was differentiated instead of integrated: integrating raises the power.
power-not-raised (procedural): It was divided by the power without raising it: xⁿ becomes xⁿ⁺¹ ⁄ (n + 1).
multiply-for-power (prerequisite): A power was worked out as a multiplication (4⁴ as 4 × 4); a power multiplies 4 by itself 4 times.
ignore-lower-limit (conceptual): Only the upper limit was used; the answer is F(upper) − F(lower).

teach.idea: An antiderivative of xⁿ is xⁿ⁺¹ ⁄ (n + 1).
teach.method: Raise the power, divide by the new power, then F(upper) − F(lower).

families.title: An integral by substitution
explanations: limits-not-changed (procedural): The old limits were used for u: when x goes from 2 to 3, u = x² + 4 goes from 8 to 13.
no-divide (procedural): The power was raised but not divided by: ∫ uⁿ du = uⁿ⁺¹ ⁄ (n + 1).
extra-half (conceptual): It was divided by 2 for du = 2x dx, but the 2x is already in the integral: 2x dx is exactly du.
multiply-for-power (prerequisite): A power was worked out as a multiplication (12⁴ as 12 × 4); a power multiplies 12 by itself 4 times.

teach.idea: With u = x² + c, 2x dx becomes du.
teach.method: Change the limits to u, integrate uⁿ, and evaluate between the u limits.

families.title: How many real solutions a quadratic has
explanations: negative-square (prerequisite): b² was taken as negative for a negative b; a square is never negative.
minus-c-sign (prerequisite): The sign of −4ac was lost when c is negative: − 4 × (a negative number) adds.
forgot-four (procedural): The discriminant was taken as b² − c; it is b² − 4ac.

teach.idea: b² − 4ac decides how many real solutions there are.
teach.method: Positive: two; zero: one; negative: none.

families.title: The perimeter of a rectangle
explanations: area-for-perimeter (conceptual): The space inside (area) was found; the perimeter is the distance around the edge.
two-sides-only (procedural): Only two sides were added; a rectangle has four sides, two of each length.
three-sides (procedural): One side was left out; go all the way around: four sides.

teach.idea: The perimeter is the distance all the way around a shape: add the lengths of every side.
teach.method: A rectangle has two lengths and two widths: add one length and one width, then double.

families.title: Multiplying a two-digit number by a one-digit number
explanations: tens-as-ones (conceptual): The tens digit was multiplied as if it were 9, not 90: each digit's place value counts.
fact-slip (prerequisite): A multiplication fact (9 × 9) is not yet reliable.
lost-carry (procedural): The tens carried from the ones were not added: they belong in the tens column.

teach.idea: Split the two-digit number into tens and ones, multiply each part, then add.
teach.method: 47 × 6 = 40 × 6 + 7 × 6 = 240 + 42 = 282. The 4 tens of 42 join the tens.

families.title: The remainder of a division
explanations: quotient-as-remainder (conceptual): The number of groups was given; the remainder is what is left over after the groups.
remainder-too-big (procedural): One group too few was taken: a remainder is always less than 8.
fact-slip (prerequisite): A multiplication fact (12 × 8) is not yet reliable.

teach.idea: Dividing makes equal groups; the remainder is what is left when no more full groups fit.
teach.method: Find the biggest multiple of the divisor that fits, then subtract it from the number.

families.title: Dividing a number exactly
explanations: digits-reversed (procedural): The digits of the answer were written in the wrong order: the first step gives the tens.
one-group-off (recall): A multiplication fact with 9 slipped by one group.
dropped-zero (procedural): A zero in the answer was left out: when the divisor does not go into a step, write 0 there.

teach.idea: Dividing undoes multiplying: 84 ÷ 4 asks how many 4s make 84.
teach.method: Take away a large, easy chunk first (20 × 4 = 80), then divide what is left (4 ÷ 4 = 1): 20 + 1 = 21.

families.title: A fraction times a whole number
explanations: multiply-both (conceptual): Top and bottom were both multiplied by 9: that gives an equal fraction, not 9 lots of it.
multiply-bottom (procedural): The bottom was multiplied; 9 lots of 11/12 is 9 × 11 pieces of the same size.
add-whole (conceptual): 9 was added to the top; multiplying means 9 lots.

teach.idea: k × a/b means k lots of a/b: the pieces stay the same size, there are just more of them.
teach.method: Multiply the top by k and keep the bottom: 3 × 2/7 = 6/7.

families.title: Adding fractions with different denominators
explanations: add-tops-and-bottoms (conceptual): Tops and bottoms were added separately; fractions with different pieces must first be written with the same pieces.
same-bottom-not-scaled (procedural): A common denominator was chosen but the tops were not changed to match it.

teach.idea: Fractions can be added only when they count the same size of piece.
teach.method: Write both with a common denominator (an equivalent fraction for each), then add the tops.

families.title: A percentage of an amount
explanations: no-hundred (conceptual): Per cent means out of 100: the amount must be divided by 100 as well as multiplied.
percent-as-divisor (conceptual): It was divided by 95; 95% means 95 out of every 100.
subtracted (procedural): 95% of 400 is a part of 400, not 400 minus 95.

teach.idea: Per cent means out of 100: 30% of an amount is 30 parts of every 100.
teach.method: Find 1% (divide by 100) or 10% (divide by 10), then build up: 30% of 200 = 3 × 20 = 60.

families.title: The mean of four numbers
explanations: total-not-shared (procedural): The numbers were added but the total was not shared out among the four.
divide-by-three (procedural): The total was divided by the wrong count: there are four numbers.
middle-for-mean (conceptual): A middle value was chosen; the mean shares the total equally.

teach.idea: The mean shares the total out equally: it is the value every number would have if they were levelled out.
teach.method: Add all the numbers, then divide by how many numbers there are.

families.title: The square root of a perfect square
explanations: squared-instead (conceptual): The number was squared; the square root goes the other way.
near-square (recall): A square fact next to the right one was used.
half-for-root (conceptual): The number was halved; the square root is the number that multiplied by itself gives it.

teach.idea: A square root undoes squaring: √49 is the number that, multiplied by itself, makes 49.
teach.method: Think of the square facts: 7 × 7 = 49, so √49 = 7.

families.title: The volume of a cuboid in unit cubes
explanations: one-layer (conceptual): Only the bottom layer was counted; there are as many layers as the height.
added-sides (conceptual): The three lengths were added; volume multiplies them.
outside-only (conceptual): The squares on the outside faces were counted; volume counts the cubes inside too.

teach.idea: Volume counts the cubes that fill a shape: layers of cubes stacked up.
teach.method: Count one layer (length × width), then multiply by the number of layers (the height).

families.title: Solving ax + b = c
explanations: forgot-divide (procedural): 20 was taken away but the 9 was not divided out: 9x = 108 means x = 108 ÷ 9.
added-not-subtracted (procedural): 18 was added to both sides; to undo + 18, subtract 18.
divided-first (procedural): Only part of the left side was divided: undo the + 18 first, then the × 9.

teach.idea: An equation is a balance: do the same to both sides and it stays true.
teach.method: Undo the operations in reverse order: first take away the number added, then divide by the number multiplying x.

families.title: A direct proportion
explanations: additive (conceptual): The difference in pencils was added to the price; in a proportion every pencil costs the same, so the price is multiplied.
no-unit (procedural): The total for 8 was multiplied by 12; first find the price of one pencil.

teach.idea: In a direct proportion, twice as many costs twice as much: the price of one stays the same.
teach.method: Find the cost of one (divide), then multiply by how many you want.

families.title: Factorising x² + px + q
explanations: sum-minus-product (procedural): The number was found from the product alone, with the wrong sign: the two numbers must multiply to q AND add to p.
coefficient-as-number (conceptual): The x coefficient was copied into the bracket; the two numbers in the brackets add up to it.
constant-minus (procedural): The given number was taken away from the constant; the two numbers multiply to the constant.

teach.idea: (x + m)(x + n) = x² + (m + n)x + mn: the two numbers multiply to the constant and add to the x coefficient.
teach.method: List pairs that multiply to the constant; choose the pair that adds to the x coefficient. Watch the signs.

families.title: The nth term of an arithmetic progression
explanations: n-jumps (procedural): 20 jumps were counted; from term 1 to term 20 there are 19 jumps.
times-n (conceptual): The first term was multiplied; an arithmetic progression adds the same difference each time.
forgot-start (procedural): Only the jumps were counted; the sequence starts at the first term.

teach.idea: Each term of an arithmetic progression is the one before plus the common difference d.
teach.method: Term n = first term + (n − 1) × d: count the jumps, not the terms.

families.title: The distance between two points
explanations: added-sides (conceptual): The across and up distances were added; the straight distance is the hypotenuse: √(across² + up²).
no-root (procedural): The square root was not taken at the end.
sign-slip (prerequisite): A difference of coordinates lost a sign: from −2 to 3 is 5, not 1.

teach.idea: The distance between two points is the hypotenuse of a right triangle whose sides are the across and up distances.
teach.method: Find across and up (differences of coordinates), square them, add, and take the square root.

families.title: The highest common factor
explanations: lcm-for-hcf (conceptual): The lowest common multiple was found; the HCF is the largest number that divides both.
a-common-factor (conceptual): A common factor was found, but not the highest one.
difference (procedural): The difference was given; keep going: the HCF also divides the difference, so repeat with the smaller numbers.

teach.idea: The HCF is the largest number that divides both exactly. Euclid: it also divides their difference and the remainder.
teach.method: Divide the larger by the smaller and keep the remainder; repeat with the smaller number and the remainder until the remainder is 0.

families.title: A 2 × 2 determinant
explanations: added-diagonals (procedural): The two diagonal products were added; the determinant subtracts them: ad − bc.
reversed (procedural): The products were subtracted the wrong way round: ad − bc, not bc − ad.
wrong-pairs (procedural): The wrong entries were paired: multiply along the diagonals, a × d and b × c.

teach.idea: The determinant of [[a, b], [c, d]] is ad − bc: the product down one diagonal minus the product down the other.
teach.method: Multiply top-left by bottom-right, multiply top-right by bottom-left, and subtract the second from the first. Keep the signs.

families.title: A limit that needs factorising
explanations: zero-for-undefined (conceptual): 0 ⁄ 0 was taken as 0; it means the expression must be simplified first (factorise and cancel).
forgot-plus-a (procedural): x² − a² was factorised as (x − a) alone; it is (x − a)(x + a), which gives 2a at x = a.
squared (procedural): x² − a² was replaced by x²; after cancelling, (x + a) gives 2a.

teach.idea: When substituting gives 0 ⁄ 0, the limit still exists: simplify first, then substitute.
teach.method: Factorise x² − a² = (x − a)(x + a), cancel (x − a), then put x = a.

families.title: A conditional probability from a table
explanations: whole-class (conceptual): The whole class was counted; given that a girl is chosen, only the girls count.
not-over-yes (procedural): Chess girls were compared with non-chess girls; a probability divides by all the girls.
reversed-condition (conceptual): The chess club was taken as the group; the question is among the girls.

teach.idea: P(A given B) counts only the cases where B happened: B becomes the whole.
teach.method: Find the group you are told about (the girls), then the fraction of that group with the property (in the chess club).
